theorem_title: All original-band bank spans fit the encoder envelope
theorem_formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.SourceBandBanksCosts.span_count_le_encoderCount {G n : ℕ} (hG : G ≤ _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.CostLedger.bandCount n) :
    G*_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.SourceBandBankLayout.span (_root_.ThreeSum.Scales.microHalf (_root_.ThreeSum.Scales.inputBits n)) (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.Scales.blockCount (_root_.ThreeSum.Scales.inputBits n)) (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.Scales.mu n) ≤
      _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.SourceBandBanksCosts.storageFactor n*_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.StageBounds.encoderCount n := by sorry
theorem_natural_language_statement:
Let $G,n\in\mathbb N$ with $G$ no greater than the cost-ledger band count. Evaluate $h,J,c$ at the executable half-size, block count, and inner size for $n$. Then $$G\operatorname{span}(h,J,c)\le\operatorname{storageFactor}(n)\operatorname{encoderCount}(n).$$

Bounds persistent source-bank storage by the encoder-count envelope. This supports the complete deterministic integer 3SUM runtime proof.
